meal.title: Understand three‑tier architecture
meal.objective: Explain how UI, back‑end, and database are separated into layers

voice.script: Why does a grocery app need three separate layers? How do UI, back‑end, and database stay separate? Imagine the checkout screen, the order logic, and the inventory table all talking directly. That quickly becomes a tangled mess. In a three tier architecture we split responsibilities. The user interface, or UI, handles what the shopper sees and clicks. The back‑end processes requests, applies business rules, and talks to storage. The database stores product data, prices, and stock levels. Each layer communicates only with the one below it, so changes in the UI don’t break the database, and the back‑end can be reused across different front‑ends. This separation makes the app easier to develop, test, and scale.
